text:
## Abstract  
The prevalence of carbapenem-related studies among *Escherichia coli* sequencing runs was quantified in the European Nucleotide Archive (ENA). Two programmatic queries were issued through BRC Analytics’ federated ENA tools: (i) `brc_ena_runs` to count all *E. coli* runs (taxon ID 562) and (ii) `brc_ena_search` with `title_contains="carbapenem"` to count the subset whose study titles mention “carbapenem.” A total of 551 679 *E. coli* runs were recorded in ENA, of which 9 759 referenced carbapenems. The resulting fraction is 1.77 %. Knowing the scale of carbapenem-focused *E. coli* sequencing informs researchers and public-health analysts about the relative representation of antimicrobial-resistance studies within the current global sequence repository.

## I. Introduction  
Background. Carbapenem-resistant *Escherichia coli* poses a critical threat to public health because carbapenems are often last-resort antibiotics. Sequencing data in ENA provide insights into the genomic basis and epidemiology of such resistance.  
Literature Review. No literature was retrieved for this query.  
Knowledge Gap. The proportion of *E. coli* sequencing runs in ENA that explicitly reference carbapenems had not been quantified.  
Objective & Hypothesis. We aimed to determine what fraction of all *E. coli* ENA runs explicitly mention “carbapenem” in their study titles. We hypothesised that the fraction would be small (<5 %), reflecting that only a subset of sequencing projects focus on carbapenem resistance.

## II. Materials and Methods  
Study Design. A descriptive database audit of ENA run metadata for *E. coli* was performed.  
Materials.  
• ENA portal accessed via BRC Analytics tools:  
  – `brc_ena_runs` (all runs)  
  – `brc_ena_search` (carbapenem-keyword subset)  
Procedures.  
1. Total *E. coli* runs  
   Tool: `brc_ena_runs`  
   Arguments: `taxonomy_id="562"`, `limit=1` (returns count)  
2. Carbapenem-mention runs  
   Tool: `brc_ena_search`  
   Arguments: `taxonomy_id="562"`, `title_contains="carbapenem"`, `limit=1` (returns count).  
Statistical Analysis. Counts were read from the `total_in_ena` (all runs) and `total_matching` (keyword runs) fields. Fraction = (total carbapenem runs / total runs) × 100.

## III. Results  
Table 1. Counts of *E. coli* ENA runs and carbapenem-related subset.

| Category | Runs (n) | Proportion (%) |
|----------|---------:|---------------:|
| All *E. coli* runs | 551 679 | — |
| Runs with “carbapenem” in study title | 9 759 | 1.77 |

Findings. Among 551 679 *E. coli* sequencing runs in ENA, 9 759 runs had study titles containing the term “carbapenem,” representing 1.77 % of the total.

## IV. Discussion  
Interpretation. Approximately one in fifty-six *E. coli* sequencing runs archived in ENA explicitly reference carbapenems, suggesting a modest but non-negligible focus on carbapenem resistance within deposited datasets.  
Context. The finding provides a quantitative baseline for researchers planning meta-analyses of carbapenem resistance in *E. coli* and highlights the availability of nearly 10 000 relevant runs for downstream genomic investigations.  
Limitations. The keyword search was limited to the `study_title` field; runs addressing carbapenems without the term in the title were not captured, potentially underestimating the true fraction. ENA metadata are author-supplied and may vary in completeness or spelling.  
Conclusion & Future Directions. Carbapenem-related *E. coli* runs constitute 1.77 % of the ENA corpus. Future work should expand keyword sets (e.g. specific carbapenem names or resistance genes) and inspect sample attributes to refine the estimate.

## References  
[1] ENA portal search via BRC Analytics. https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/portal/api/search?query=tax_eq(562)%20AND%20study_title=%22*carbapenem*%22&limit=1  
[2] ENA taxonomy run count via BRC Analytics. https://brc-analytics.org/api/v1/ena/taxonomy/562?limit=1  

## Acknowledgments  
We acknowledge the European Nucleotide Archive (ENA) and BRC Analytics for providing programmatic access to sequencing-run metadata.
